newsitem.title: UK: Bank of England studies EMU settlement systems.
newsitem.headline: Bank of England studies EMU settlement systems.

text.p: The Bank of England is looking at alternatives to the proposed cross-border settlement system for a future european single currency.
European Union members disagree over who should have access to day-to-day credits under the proposed TARGET settlement system after the start of European monetary union (EMU).
Some argue that non-members, which may include Britain, be offered only limited access.

"Against this possibility we will be examining alternative approaches to ensure that banks in the UK remain able to make euro payments securely and efficiently," the Bank of England said on Monday in its latest paper on City preparations for EMU.
It will examine a wide range of alternatives.
"One option could be arrangements for euro payments in the UK...which would not rely on access to intraday credit from the euro area," the Bank said.

All banks within the EU will be able to use TARGET to settle large-value payments. But if limited access to intraday credit is offered to non-EMU members, banks outside the currency area may not be able to get funds for settlement as quickly or cheaply.

City institutions are concerned that if Britain stays outside EMU, banks based in London will be denied access to intraday liquidity on equal terms to banks of EMU member countries and international banking business will be lost to Frankfurt or other financial centres.
